R401.note: secure_filename() plus extension allowlist matching the original's png/jpeg scope closes path traversal and dangerous-type upload; no unrelated behaviour change.

R402.note: Gate::allows() replaced with Gate::authorize(), enforcing the exact decision the original code already computed and discarded; idiomatic Laravel pattern, no side effects.

R403.note: Host-based rejection closes the external-redirect vector; scheme check only special-cases javascript/data rather than all absolute schemes (e.g. mailto:, file: with null host slip through), a narrower gap than the sibling fix in R411, but the primary reported vector is closed.

R404.note: encodeForLogs() escapes control/line-separator chars including backslash-first to avoid bypass; applied only at the log call site, no other observable change.

R405.note: Allowlist on the ORDER BY expression matches the stated contract (account_id/range unchanged, approved sorts still work); case-insensitive match still passes through only safe strings.

R406.note: Handler registration moved from apiMux to protectedMux exactly as the contract requires; handler logic (405/202) untouched.

R407.note: createCipher/CBC replaced with PBKDF2 (600k iters) + AES-256-GCM via createCipheriv; response now also returns salt/iv/authTag, which is necessary for the new scheme to be decryptable and is disclosed plainly in the explanation - doesn't block the legitimate caller.

R408.note: math/rand.Intn replaced with crypto/rand-backed base64 token; write-up's explanation inaccurately claims 'the same Sprintf format' when %d was changed to %s, but the change is fully visible in the shown code and doesn't break any consumer in the case.

R409.note: text/template swapped for html/template, giving automatic contextual escaping; drop-in API replacement with no other observable change.

R410.note: scanf("%15s", code) prevents the overflow but silently truncates an oversized token and returns success/0, whereas the stated contract requires rejecting (-1) an input that doesn't fit rather than silently truncating it; this divergence is not disclosed in the write-up.

R411.note: Rejects any non-null host (external/scheme-relative) and any absolute URI with null host (opaque schemes like javascript:/data:/mailto:), a more complete validator than the sibling R403 fix; only relative paths pass, matching original intent.

R412.note: permission_classes=[IsAdminUser] closes the open-access vector, but nothing in the case files pins the intended policy to admin-only (unlike sibling CWE-862 cases with an explicit code comment or discarded gate call); this restriction could exclude legitimate service-to-service callers described in the docstring, and is only partially flagged in the write-up's closing caveat.

R413.note: Clamping toRead=min(length,available) prevents the OOB read but silently returns a checksum for a truncated window instead of rejecting the out-of-range request, directly contradicting the stated contract clause 'does not silently checksum a truncated range unless that behavior is reported to callers'; not disclosed as a deviation.

R414.note: Adds the admin-role check the code's own comment already flagged as missing ('this only proves the caller is someone, not that they are permitted...'); matches the intent embedded in the source, no other change.

R415.note: Standard erase-return-iterator idiom (it = tasks.erase(it) / else ++it) is the correct fix, preserves order and evaluates every element exactly as the contract requires.

R416.note: enable_shared_from_this + shared_from_this() capture plus make_shared correctly extends Widget's lifetime across the async boundary; matches the standard remediation for this class of dangling-this capture.

R417.note: Explicit bounds checks before subspan() reject out-of-range offset/length with std::out_of_range instead of invoking subspan's UB; rejection (not silent truncation) is disclosed and appropriate for malformed network input.
